name: Gabby Giffords

lean.basis: Switched from Republican to Democrat in 2000; in Congress she was a moderate and a member of the Blue Dog and New Democrat coalitions.
Since 2013 her gun-safety group has backed Democrats, including $15 million to help Kamala Harris in 2024.

sources.title: Giffords group commits $15 million to help Harris beat Trump — NBC News

race_2028.basis: Kelly's wife; he says he has been discussing a 2028 run with her and will decide after the 2026 midterms.

sources.title: Mark Kelly on a presidential decision — KTAR News
Mark Kelly to make decision on presidential run after midterms — Deseret News

current_role: Co-founder of Giffords, a gun-safety group; former U.S. representative from Arizona
summary: Gabby Giffords served in the Arizona legislature (2001–2005) and the U.S. House (2007–2012), resigning after she was shot in a 2011 assassination attempt in Tucson. With her husband, Mark Kelly, she founded the gun-safety group now called Giffords in 2013. Biden awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2022.

timeline.role: Arizona state representative, then state senator
